Steckwürfeln Rules

Roll two dice and peg the holes numbered 2 to 12; the fewest points win.

The rules

The holes
There are eleven holes numbered 2 to 12. At the start of a turn no hole has a peg.
A turn
Roll two dice. Either put one peg into the hole with the total, or two pegs into the holes of the two single dice - with a 2 and a 4 that is hole 6, or holes 2 and 4. A hole takes one peg only. With two equal dice (3 and 3) only the total counts, and there is no hole 1.
Going on
Keep rolling and pegging as long as a peg fits. When a roll cannot be pegged, the turn is over: add up the numbers of the free holes. That is your score.
Double six
Double six is a joker, and players agree what it means. Here you choose: roll again (nothing is pegged), the turn ends at once, or no special rule - then 6 and 6 pegs hole 12 like any other total.
Winning
After the chosen number of rounds the fewest points in total win; equal points are a draw. Pegging all eleven holes gives 0 points and wins at once.
Shared board
In this variant all players use one board and roll once per turn. Whoever cannot peg any more is out; the last player left wins.
The computer
On its own board it pegs the way that keeps the most later rolls playable. On a shared board it does the opposite: it leaves the next player as few playable rolls as it can.
Help
Undo takes back your last pegging. There is no time limit.
